sentence: Decades ago, two of the world's great ant scientists sat down with this exact sum, and decided the scale would roughly balance.
claim: In 1994, Bert Hölldobler and E. O. Wilson estimated about 10^16 ants alive at once and that all ants together weigh about as much as all humans.
source_title: B. Hölldobler & E. O. Wilson, Journey to the Ants (1994), as quoted: 'all ants in the world weigh about as much as all humans'; BBC More or Less analysis of the claim
note: Excerpts: the claim 'was originally made by … Edward O. Wilson and … Bert Hoelldobler in their 1994 book Journey To The Ants'; 'ten thousand trillion (10^16) live ants'. The names and year are on screen (label); the voice says 'two of the world's great ant scientists'. 'Sat down with this exact sum' is fair: their figure was a back-of-the-envelope estimate (1% of C. B. Williams' insect count).

sentence: Then a team gathered hundreds of real ant counts, from forests, deserts and cities, and found about twice as many ants as anyone had guessed.
claim: Schultheiss et al. (2022) compiled 489 field studies of ground-dwelling ant counts across biomes and estimated about 20 × 10^15 ants: about twice the 1994 figure.
source_title: P. Schultheiss et al., 'The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth', PNAS 119, e2201550119 (2022) (DOI from memory: a person confirms it when opening the link)
note: Excerpts: 'estimates came from 465 studies' (Phys.org) / 489 studies (the paper's abstract, to be confirmed by a person); 'the total number of ants on Earth is estimated to be 2 to 20 times' earlier estimates. Computed: 2e16 / 1e16 = 2×. 'Hundreds of real ant counts' covers both numbers.

sentence: But a real ant is tinier than the old guess assumed, and once they're weighed properly, all of them together come to only about a fifth of us.
claim: Ants' total biomass is about 12 megatonnes of carbon (dry carbon), using measured mean worker weights.
source_title: P. Schultheiss et al., 'The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth', PNAS 119, e2201550119 (2022) (DOI from memory: a person confirms it when opening the link)
note: Excerpt: 'a dry carbon biomass of 12 megatonnes'; 'mean worker weight measured from a selection of species'. 'A real ant is tinier than the old guess assumed': the 1994 balance needed an average ant of roughly 60 mg (BBC's back-calculation); real common workers weigh 1–2 mg fresh (Ratnieks, quoted by the BBC).

sentence: But a real ant is tinier than the old guess assumed, and once they're weighed properly, all of them together come to only about a fifth of us.
claim: 12 Mt of ant carbon is about 20% of humanity's 60 Mt (0.06 Gt C).
source_title: Y. M. Bar-On, R. Phillips & R. Milo, 'The biomass distribution on Earth', PNAS 115, 6506 (2018)
note: Computed: 12 / 60 = 0.20. Schultheiss et al. state the same: 'about 20% of the global human biomass'. Said as 'about a fifth'.

sentence: That's still more than every wild bird and mammal on Earth combined.
claim: Ants' biomass exceeds the combined biomass of all wild birds and wild mammals.
source_title: P. Schultheiss et al., 'The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth', PNAS 119, e2201550119 (2022) (DOI from memory: a person confirms it when opening the link)
note: Excerpt: 'actually exceeds the combined biomass of all wild birds and wild mammals'. 'Wild' is on screen (the third pan's label).

sentence: And for each one of us, there are about two and a half million ants.
claim: About 2 × 10^16 ants for 8.2 billion people is about 2.4 million ants per person; said and shown as 'about two and a half million' (to the nearest half million).
source_title: How many ants are on Earth? 20 quadrillion, study says (Phys.org, 2022)
note: Computed: 2e16 / 8.2e9 = 2.44e+06. Said as 'about two and a half million'.

sentence: Take the heaviest estimate anyone has published, and we still win the scale.
claim: Published estimates of global ant biomass span about 3.6–50 Mt of carbon; even the highest is about 83% of humanity's 60 Mt.
source_title: T. M. Fayle & P. Klimeš, 'Improving estimates of global ant biomass and abundance', PNAS commentary (2022), PMC9586285
note: Excerpt (the PNAS commentary): the full range of published ant biomass estimates is roughly 3.6 to 50 Mt. Computed: 50 / 60 = 0.83. The sensitivity line.

sentence: But they win on the count.
claim: By weight humans outweigh ants about five to one; by number ants outnumber humans about 2.4 million to one.
source_title: P. Schultheiss et al., 'The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth', PNAS 119, e2201550119 (2022) (DOI from memory: a person confirms it when opening the link)
note: The takeaway restates c4 and c6; 'by a lot' = about five times.

sentence: And for each one of us, there are about two and a half million ants.
claim: The world's population is about 8.2 billion (mid-2024), the divisor in c6's 2e16 ÷ 8.2e9 ≈ 2.44 million ants a person.
source_title: World Population Prospects 2024 (UN DESA Population Division); news.un.org/en/story/2024/07/1151971
note: The same source and figure as No. 002's c1.
